title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.

Exactly one pair adds up to target, and you may not use the same element twice. Print the two indices in increasing order, separated by a space.

Input format
Line 1: n, the length of nums
Line 2: n space-separated integers
Line 3: target

Constraints
2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
-10^9 ≤ nums[i], target ≤ 10^9

visibleTestCases.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] = 2 + 7 = 9, so the answer is 0 1.
Both elements are used once each.

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string s containing only the characters ( ) { } [ and ], decide whether it is valid.

A string is valid when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, and brackets are closed in the correct order. Print true or false.

Input format
Line 1: the string s

Constraints
1 ≤ |s| ≤ 10^5

visibleTestCases.explanation: One pair, closed correctly.
Three pairs side by side.
( is closed by ], which is the wrong type.

title: Reverse Linked List
description:
Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.

The input is read into a linked list for you, and the reversed list is printed as space-separated values.

Input format
Line 1: n, the number of nodes
Line 2: n space-separated node values

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
-5000 ≤ value ≤ 5000

visibleTestCases.explanation: The list 1→2→3→4→5 becomes 5→4→3→2→1.
The list 1→2 becomes 2→1.
A single node is already reversed.

title: Binary Search
description:
Given a sorted array of distinct integers nums and a target, return the index of target in nums, or -1 if it isn't there.

Your solution should run in O(log n) time.

Input format
Line 1: n
Line 2: n sorted, distinct integers
Line 3: target

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
-10^9 ≤ nums[i], target ≤ 10^9

visibleTestCases.explanation: 9 is at index 4.
2 is not in the array, so the answer is -1.

title: Climbing Stairs
description:
You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can climb either 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?

Input format
Line 1: n

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 45

visibleTestCases.explanation: Two ways: 1+1, or 2.
Three ways: 1+1+1, 1+2, or 2+1.

title: Maximum Subarray
description:
Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) with the largest sum, and print that sum.

Input format
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
-10^4 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^4

visibleTestCases.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum, 6.
The only subarray is [1].
The whole array sums to 23.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.

Input format
Line 1: the string s (letters, digits and symbols, no spaces)

Constraints
1 ≤ |s| ≤ 5 × 10^4

visibleTestCases.explanation: The answer is "abc", with length 3.
The answer is "b", with length 1.
The answer is "wke", with length 3. "pwke" is a subsequence, not a substring.

title: Number of Islands
description:
Given an r × c grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), count the islands.

An island is a group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically, surrounded by water. Everything outside the grid is water.

Input format
Line 1: r and c
Next r lines: a string of c characters, each 0 or 1

Constraints
1 ≤ r, c ≤ 300

visibleTestCases.explanation: All the land is connected, so there is 1 island.
Three separate groups of land: top-left, the middle cell and bottom-right.

title: Coin Change
description:
You are given coins of different denominations and a total amount. Return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount, or -1 if it can't be made.

You have an unlimited supply of each coin.

Input format
Line 1: n, the number of coin types
Line 2: n coin values
Line 3: amount

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 12
1 ≤ coins[i] ≤ 2^31 - 1
0 ≤ amount ≤ 10^4

visibleTestCases.explanation: 11 = 5 + 5 + 1, which uses 3 coins.
An odd amount can never be made from 2s.
Zero coins make an amount of 0.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip elements. Aim for O(n log n).

Input format
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
-10^9 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^9

visibleTestCases.explanation: One longest subsequence is [2, 3, 7, 101], so the length is 4.
[0, 1, 2, 3] has length 4.
Equal values are not strictly increasing, so the answer is 1.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where each bar has width 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

Input format
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated heights

Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 2 × 10^4
0 ≤ height[i] ≤ 10^5

visibleTestCases.explanation: Water collects in the dips between the bars: 6 units in total.
9 units of water are trapped.

title: Edit Distance
description:
Given two words, return the minimum number of operations needed to convert the first into the second.

You may insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character. Each counts as one operation.

Input format
Line 1: word1
Line 2: word2
Words are made of lowercase letters. An empty word is written as a single dash (-).

Constraints
0 ≤ |word1|, |word2| ≤ 500

visibleTestCases.explanation: horse → rorse (replace h), rorse → rose (delete r), rose → ros (delete e): 3 operations.
Five operations turn intention into execution.
